Handoff below — written as normal prose for pasting into the incident channel or ticket.

---

# Incident Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status at handoff:** ONGOING. Not mitigated. Errors were still firing at the last log line (2026-03-14T03:59:27Z). No recovery observed.

## Root cause

Gateway config generation 119 enabled connection-per-request on a connection pool that was never resized for it:

```
2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z INFO  config  generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed
2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
```

With `perRequest: true`, every inbound request takes its own upstream connection instead of sharing. The pool holds 20. Concurrency exceeded 20 almost immediately and never came back down. The raised upstream timeout (2000ms → 2500ms) makes it worse by holding each connection longer before release.

Every failure is the same error, 530 occurrences, no other error code in the log:

```
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

`in_use` is pinned at 20/20 in every single instance. The queue depth grows from 13 waiters to 271, and request latency grows 659ms → 850ms, so this was degrading steadily, not stable.

## Impact window

- **Start:** 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z, first failure `req-07401`. That is 37 seconds after the config applied and 19 seconds after deploy dep-4471 finished.
- **End:** unknown. Log ends 2026-03-14T03:59:27Z with the failure rate unchanged. Minimum duration 1h 45m.
- **Rate:** steady 5 failures to 1 success per minute for the entire window, 530 total 503s.
- **Affected routes:** `/v1/session`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/cart` — 106 failures each. All revenue-path traffic.
- **Upstreams:** evenly spread (catalog-svc 133, accounts-svc 133, orders-svc 132, billing-svc 132). No single bad backend; the fault is gateway-side.

**Detection gap worth fixing:** `/health` was the only route still returning 200, with `pool_wait=2ms` throughout. Health probes stayed green through a total outage of real traffic. On-call was not paged until 2026-03-14T03:21:05Z — 67 minutes after the first 503 — and only then on error rate:

```
2026-03-14T03:21:05.282Z WARN  ops  paged on-call: error_rate 5m avg is 71%
```

## Roll back

**dep-4471.**

```
dep-4471,gateway,2026-03-14T02:12:00Z,2026-03-14T02:14:00Z,a.novak,config: connection-per-request for pool isolation
```

Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`. Reverting `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` to 2000 is optional and secondary — it aggravates the exhaustion but is not the cause. If the pool-isolation behaviour is genuinely needed, do not re-enable it until the pool is sized well above peak concurrency; 20 is not enough.

**Deploys ruled out:** dep-4468 (catalog-svc, 22:04Z) and dep-4469 (accounts-svc, 23:31Z) are hours early with clean traffic after. dep-4470 (worker, 00:48Z) is not in the gateway request path. dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) both shipped *during* the outage and cannot have caused it — but note they were deployed into an active incident, so confirm neither is now sitting unverified behind a broken gateway.

## Separate issue — do not conflate

worker.log over the same window has **zero errors** and zero failed jobs. Workers were unaffected by the gateway problem.

However, worker job duration is climbing linearly at roughly +110ms per 10 minutes for the whole window, from 327ms average at 01:00Z to 2197ms at 03:50Z. There is no inflection at 02:14Z, and it is already climbing at the first log line, so it predates both the gateway change and the start of the log. `db_wait` is flat at 5ms average, max 12ms, so this is not database contention — the time is being spent elsewhere in the runner.

Suspect is dep-4470 (worker, 00:48–00:55Z, j.tanaka, "retry backoff for webhook jobs"), which landed just before the log window, but there is no pre-deploy baseline in this log to confirm it. Pull worker logs from before 00:48Z to prove or clear it. File this separately; it is not part of the gateway incident.

The single worker WARN is pre-existing and tracked, not related:

```
2026-03-14T02:36:22.838Z WARN  db  slow query 1.9s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = ? — unindexed scan, known issue OPS-2210
```

---

One thing to flag: you described this as starting "last night," but both logs are timestamped 2026-03-14 and today is 2026-09-01. Either these are archived logs from a past incident or the log dates are wrong — worth confirming which before anyone rolls back production on them.
